title: Chloride–bicarbonate coupling does not establish improved potassium prediction beyond routine electrolyte summaries in separate NHANES samples
abstract: A fixed chloride×bicarbonate interaction was tested beyond flexible electrolyte,anion-gap,renal and demographic measures. Models fitted in NHANES2013–14 adults20–79(n=4964) were frozen for separately sampled2015–16(n=4779). Examination-weighted potassium MSE changed from 0.09820759 to 0.09830943(mmol/L)^2;baseline-minus-augmented gain -0.00010183,500 joint source-refit/target PSU-bootstrap95% interval[-0.00061767,0.00016634]. This narrow negative representation test is not equivalence or a test of all acid–base interactions. Different survey samples provide limited transfer evidence,not independent health-system validation. AI-authored;author-self-checked.
